newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIAN CENTRAL BANK REVOKES LICENCES OF 22 BROKERAGES.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIAN CENTRAL BANK REVOKES LICENCES OF 22 BROKERAGES.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) revoked the licences of 22 brokerages for violating BNB trading rules, the central bank said in a statement.
"On grounds of violating articles in the Banking and Crediting Act, the BNB board revokes the banking operations licenses of the following financial houses," said the statement.

The 22 enumerated brokerages include Diva, Financial Brokerage House Plovdiv, GDS Financial House, Naiva-ITB Valeri Naidenov, Lex Financial house, Cash Financial House and Agrofinance in the Black Sea port of Varna,
Some 150 brokerage houses mushroomed in Bulgaria after the collapse of the communist regime and centralised economy more than six years ago.
They frequently came under fire from the central bank and the finance ministry for directly participating in the local forex market and artificially weakening the lev.

Under Bulgarian bank laws, brokerages are licensed to carry out financial operations only through the mediation of banks. They were banned from direct banking operations such as management of trust funds and dealing in government securities and operation.
"Most of these brokerages either no longer operate or were found managing trust funds," said recently a BNB official, who declined to be named.

As part of measures aimed to support the lev, which comes under severe pressure in the winter due to fuel imports, the BNB launched series of checks of financial houses last week pledging to close down those which have constantly violated its regulations.
The BNB has also launched parallel checks of the hundreds of foreign exchange bureax.
